A close reading for the week

“All the world’s a stage”

As You Like It · Act 2, Scene 7

The most quoted speech in the comedies is spoken by its most melancholy character, and the play answers it within a minute by carrying an exhausted old man on stage and giving him supper.

JaquesAll the world’s a stage,
And all the men and women merely players;1
They have their exits and their entrances,
And one man in his time plays many parts,
His acts being seven ages. At first the infant,
Mewling and puking in the nurse’s arms;2

  1. 1

    The world as a stage

    The idea that the world is a theatre was proverbial long before Shakespeare, and the Globe’s own motto is thought to have been a Latin version of it. Jaques’s contribution is “merely”: men and women are merely players, and the word drains the metaphor of dignity. The theatre here is no glorious mirror of life, only a cast of puppets going through routines. The speech’s fame has softened a sneer.

  2. 2

    The satirist’s eye

    Every age is caught in its least flattering posture: the infant “mewling and puking”, the schoolboy “whining” and “creeping like snail”, the lover “sighing like furnace” over a ballad to an eyebrow. Jaques observes humanity as a collector of specimens, from the outside, with a taxonomist’s cold accuracy. The details are funny and exact, and there is no love in any of them.
